message.content:
\[
\frac{\cos 96^\circ+\sin 96^\circ}{\cos 96^\circ-\sin 96^\circ}
\]

Using \(\sin A+\cos A\) identities, or directly:

\[
\frac{\sin\theta+\cos\theta}{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}
=\tan(\theta+45^\circ)
\]

So for \(\theta=96^\circ\),

\[
\frac{\cos96^\circ+\sin96^\circ}{\cos96^\circ-\sin96^\circ}
=\tan(96^\circ+45^\circ)=\tan141^\circ.
\]

Thus the equation is

\[
\tan(19x^\circ)=\tan141^\circ.
\]

So

\[
19x \equiv 141 \pmod{180}.
\]

We need integer \(x\), so solve

\[
19x=141+180k
\]

for integer \(k\). Then

\[
x=\frac{141+180k}{19}.
\]

For \(x\) to be an integer,

\[
141+180k\equiv 0 \pmod{19}.
\]

Since \(141\equiv 8\pmod{19}\) and \(180\equiv 9\pmod{19}\),

\[
8+9k\equiv 0\pmod{19}
\]

\[
9k\equiv 11\pmod{19}.
\]

The inverse of \(9\) modulo \(19\) is \(17\), so

\[
k\equiv 11\cdot17\equiv187\equiv16\pmod{19}.
\]

Take the smallest nonnegative \(k\), namely \(k=16\). Then

\[
x=\frac{141+180(16)}{19}
=\frac{141+2880}{19}
=\frac{3021}{19}
=159.
\]

The answer is 159.
